messages:
marie: heads-up — shadowbench bringup for tiny-ranker-v2 (int4) shows weird short-query top1 flips vs fp16. overall NDCG@10 only -0.6%, but MRR for queries <6 tokens is -4.0%. wondering if this is a formatting / candidate-ordering culprit or a true model regression. anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: can you paste a minimal repro case? short queries + few candidates usually surface tokenization/truncation issues.

marie: yes — pasted below (from eval harness run). note the candidate that used to win is now ranked 3rd.

marie: ```
query: "how to enable 2fa"
cand[0]: "Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) in Settings > Security. Steps: ..."
cand[1]: "2FA setup: go to account, choose Authenticator app -> scan QR..."
cand[2]: "Use SMS 2FA by adding phone number in profile. Note: SMS is less secure."

fp16_scores: [0.84, 0.81, 0.65]
int4_scores: [0.72, 0.78, 0.68]
```

marie: i suspect prefix-padding or null-token handling changed the first candidate embedding/priming.

josh: hmm int4 lowering of first candidate is suspicious. Did you run tokenizer-agreement check between production preproc and the eval harness? Sometimes whitespace/case normalization differs.

marie: i ran a quick token counts diff: cand0 fp16 tokens=11, int4 tokens=12 (extra BOS or leftover whitespace). Might be an anchor token inserted by a preprocessing path in the quantized build.

arjun: infra-bot just ran the consistency CI a minute ago and reported no failures, but that job doesn't cover the new quant-runtime binary. Could you run the local `rerank-compare` script with `--show-tokenization`? Command we use: `./tools/rerank-compare --gold fp16.bin --candidate int4.bin --dataset short-queries --show-tokenization`

marie: ran it. output:

marie: ```
--show-tokenization output (candidate 0)
raw: "Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) in Settings > Security. Steps: ..."
prod_preproc: "Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) in Settings > Security. Steps: ..."
harness_preproc: "\u0000Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) in Settings > Security. Steps: ..."
-> harness_preproc has a leading null (0x00) byte inserted by the quant loader.
```

sam: that explains token count + score shift. int4 loader adding a null prefix will change embeddings a lot for short inputs. Do we know which component adds it?

josh: likely the quantized tokenizer shim we added to align padding for kernel vectorization. It prepends a control byte when sequence length < 16 to maintain alignment in a microbatch. Shouldn't affect preprocessing string, though — indicates an encoding mismatch between harness and loader.

arjun: i can repro locally. quick patch: strip leading \u0000 in harness input path before tokenization. Retest?

marie: temporary patch applied — reran on the same sample and quickbench shows:

marie: ```
metrics (short-queries subset):
fp16: NDCG@10 0.912, MRR 0.721
int4 (before patch): NDCG@10 0.903, MRR 0.693
int4 (after strip): NDCG@10 0.911, MRR 0.717
```

marie: much closer now. overall delta on entire holdout moved from -0.6% NDCG to -0.05%.

sam: nice find. action items: 1) add tokenization equivalence unit test (harness vs prod loader) 2) add a sanitizer in the quant loader to reject/control non-printing prefix bytes 3) rerun full shadowbench with this fix and post results.

josh: also add an experiment to see how sensitive ranking is to single-char prefixes. small synthetic ablation: prepend/strip a '.' or null and measure MRR shift on short queries. Could be used as a test oracle in CI.

arjun: infra-bot queued a shadowbench run job: job id sb-20240327-88, dashboard: https://redwood-internal/shadowbench/sb-20240327-88 (private). Will notify when done.

marie: thanks — i'll follow up with the rerun results. also opening a tiny PR for the sanitizer. cc @sam @josh

arjun: one more note — we should document that tiny-ranker-v2 int4 build changes the token alignment strategy and mention the potential for non-printing-prefix mismatches in the onboarding playbook. saves future confusion. :memo:

marie: agreed. tagging `#eng-ml` playbook section in the PR. :+1: 

infra-bot: shadowbench job sb-20240327-88 started (expected ~45m).

marie: cool — will wait for full run but closing this short-case triage for now. thanks all! :tada:
